comparison: Both evaluate the synthspot simulator and methodological framework (C6, C51-C64). OpenEval focuses on technical validation and features; peer reviewers emphasize the reproducibility framework (Nextflow, Docker) as 'above average for a benchmarking study' and praise the simulator assessment.

Both address benchmarking scope and methodology (C4-C5, C36-C42, C65-C72). OpenEval details dataset composition and consultation with method authors; peer reviewers highlight the comprehensive evaluation framework, reproducibility infrastructure, and methodological rigor as key strengths.

Both cover evaluation metrics (C73-C76). OpenEval describes the three complementary metrics and ranking methodology in detail; peer reviewers acknowledge the metrics as part of the overall methodological framework without specific commentary.

Both address main performance findings and rankings (C77-C79). OpenEval describes the ranking results with figure references; peer reviewers explicitly affirm that RCTD, cell2location, and SpatialDWLS show strong performance, with many methods underperforming simple baselines.

Both discuss performance with dominant cell types (C82-C84, C91). OpenEval explains variability and consistency between synthetic and real data; peer reviewers acknowledge the challenge of handling both abundance and rarity, supporting the conclusions about performance in extreme scenarios.

Both address gold standard results (C85-C86). OpenEval provides methodological details about ranking approaches; peer reviewers affirm the overall performance findings including RCTD, SpatialDWLS, and cell2location as top performers.

Both evaluate rare cell type detection analysis (C98-C111). OpenEval details the AUPR-focused analysis and abundance-performance correlation; peer reviewers explicitly support conclusions about the challenge of handling both cell abundance and rarity throughout tissue samples.

Both address stability analysis with different references (C114-C125). OpenEval describes JSD methodology and findings about methods accounting for technical variability; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the significant impact of inter- and intra-dataset reference handling on performance.

Both evaluate the liver case study (C126-C148). OpenEval details the zonation-based validation and synthetic data confirmation; peer reviewers accept the case study findings as part of the thorough and rigorous comparison, noting the study addresses situational discrepancies in model performance.

Both address metric interpretation and reference dataset selection (C149-C163). OpenEval explains metric inconsistencies and robustness findings; peer reviewers implicitly support these through acknowledgment of the study's thoroughness and the importance of optimal reference data.

Both evaluate the melanoma case study (C165-C183). OpenEval describes MC data processing and qualitative validation using endothelial cell localization; peer reviewers accept the case study as demonstrating evaluation approaches for datasets lacking absolute ground truth.

Both address runtime and scalability analysis (C184-C203). OpenEval provides detailed experimental design and findings about model reuse, GPU requirements, and marker gene methods; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the importance of runtime, computing needs, and scalability as key factors for researchers.

Both summarize main findings (C210-C218). OpenEval highlights that many methods don't outperform baselines and identifies key performance factors; peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings, noting the surprising underperformance of several methods compared to baselines.

Both address consistency of findings across datasets (C213-C214). OpenEval notes concordance between real and synthetic datasets; Reviewer 1 explicitly states results are 'very concordant between real and synthetic datasets' as a key strength.

Both evaluate the impact of gene number on performance (C219-C229). OpenEval describes findings across multiple datasets and explains why marker-based methods are less affected; peer reviewers accept these observations, noting that optimal reference data is potentially most important for performance.

Both provide practical recommendations (C233-C244). OpenEval recommends RCTD, provides reference dataset guidelines, and suggests using synthspot for quality evaluation; peer reviewers accept these recommendations as following logically from the benchmarking results, noting experimental design is equally important to tool selection.

Both address computational infrastructure (C43-C44, C245, C247-C248). OpenEval describes Nextflow and Docker implementation as ensuring reproducibility; peer reviewers explicitly praise these elements as 'above average' and note the Nextflow pipeline will facilitate inclusion of new datasets and methods.

Both evaluate the resource value (C247-C248). OpenEval claims the benchmark provides a valuable resource; peer reviewers explicitly confirm it 'provides a resource for those seeking to improve or develop new deconvolution methods' and has 'potential to set the standard of benchmarks higher.'

OpenEval evaluates background claims about spatial transcriptomics and deconvolution methods (C1-C3, C13-C31) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focus on methodological contributions rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluates claims about gaps in previous benchmarking work (C32-C35) that motivate the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accept the study's motivation implicitly through their positive assessment of its contributions.

Both address limitations of existing simulators (C45-C50). OpenEval identifies specific limitations with citations; peer reviewers accept these characterizations, noting the study provides 'a fairly decent assessment of their simulator compared to other spatial omics simulators.'

OpenEval evaluates biological context for rare cell type detection (C95-C97) with supporting citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accept the importance of rare cell detection through their support of the analysis findings.

Both address context for stability analysis (C112-C113). OpenEval provides citation and rationale for why methods should handle reference variability; peer reviewers acknowledge the significant impact of reference handling on performance, supporting the importance of this analysis.

Both address biological context for melanoma case study (C164). OpenEval provides background about melanoma as a challenging test case; peer reviewers accept the case study without challenging the biological rationale.

Both evaluate the study's scope and methodological contributions (C204-C206). OpenEval summarizes the comprehensive evaluation; peer reviewers affirm the methodological rigor and note the study addresses 'biologically relevant, previously unconsidered aspects.'

Both address validation strategies (C207-C209). OpenEval describes the multi-level validation approach; peer reviewers acknowledge the study demonstrates practical evaluation approaches and thorough comparison methods.

Both address computational requirements (C230-C232). OpenEval describes the study's setup and provides recommendations for different resource levels; peer reviewers affirm the importance of runtime and computing needs as key factors for researchers in exploratory data analysis.

Both address future developments (C246). OpenEval speculates about ongoing value as new methods emerge; peer reviewers explicitly confirm the framework's utility for future method development and note the Nextflow pipeline will facilitate inclusion of new methods.
